content.text:
The campaign is finished, and I submitted **index 7** (Bi 0.34, Cu 0.27, V 0.39). At 17.6 µA it had the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured. There were 117 candidates and only three merit measurements, so I can't tell how close it is to the best composition in the library.

| Index | Composition (Bi / Cu / V) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 0.34 / 0.27 / 0.39 | **17.6 µA** |
| 2 | 0.41 / 0.19 / 0.40 | 11.8 µA |
| 33 | 0.11 / 0.70 / 0.19 | 0.03 µA |

- **Why I started at index 2:** it has equal Bi and V and the least Cu of any candidate, making it the closest match to BiVO₄. BiVO₄ is a known visible-light photoanode, and the 2.72 eV (455 nm) light is enough to excite it.
- **Index 33 as a check:** I measured this Cu-rich composition to test the opposite corner. It gave almost no photocurrent, which pointed the last measurement back toward the Bi–V region.
- **Final pick:** the Gaussian-process model suggested index 7. It has a little more V than Bi, and it beat index 2.

I didn't use any of the five XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are present is an assumption, not something I confirmed.
